entries.title: Isaiah 57:1
segments:
Perisheth; dies. 
 
  Taken away from the evil to come; compare

. 
 
When iniquity abounds in a nation, and the righteous become few, it is a sign that evil days are at hand.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:2
segments: Shall rest in their beds; that is, in their tombs.
The rest of the body in the grave, is an emblem of the higher rest of the soul in heaven.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:3
segments: Sons of the sorceress--seed of the adulterer; race of sorcerers and adulterers; as wicked man are called the children of the devil.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:4
segments:
Draw out the tongue; thrust it out in derision. 
 
God's faithful servants must be content to bear the scorn and derision of the ungodly, for so did they treat the prophets and apostles of old, and Christ himself, the Lord of prophets and apostles.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:5
segments: Slaying the children; sacrificing them to idols.  This sin, as well as sorcery and idolatry, was practised by Manasseh, to whose reign many refer the present description.  See

. 
 
vv 5-12. 
 
The root of idolatry, with all its abominations, is "an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God."  It is because men have neither love for God's service, nor faith in his presence and power, that they multiply their efforts to find salvation by their own devices--only to sink deeper in misery and ruin.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:6
segments:
Smooth stones; these seem to have been stones set up in the valleys as objects of idolatrous worship. 
 
  Stream; that is, torrent-bed, like that of the valley of Hinnom, which was the seat of idolatrous rites.
Thy portion--thy lot; thou hast chosen them and not God for thy portion.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:7
segments: Lofty and high mountain; high places were selected by the ancients for sacrifices, whether to the true God,
or, as here to idols,
Set thy bed; idolatry is described as spiritual adultery; a common figure with the prophets.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:8
segments:
Doors--posts; of thy house. 
 
  Thy remembrance; the image of thy idol. 
 
  Gone up; upon thy bed.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:9
segments: To the king; probably the king of Egypt.

The mention of "messengers" shows that a heathen prince is meant, whose alliance Judah sought in an idolatrous spirit. 
 
  With ointment; as a present.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:10
segments:
In the greatness of thy way; in the multitude of thy journeys to obtain foreign aid. 
 
  Found the life of thy hand; found thy hand still strong for further effort. 
 
  Grieved; rather, "weakened," exhausted with toil.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:11
segments:
Of whom; of what foreign foe.  The fear of the Jews, which led them to seek help from the worship of false gods and the alliance of heathen kings, was unreasonable; since their covenant God was almighty, and faithful to his engagements. 
 
  Lied; been false to me. 
 
  Held my peace; borne thy waywardness in silence. 
 
  Thou fearest me not; the result of my forbearance is only thy continued sinfulness.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:12
segments: Thy righteousness; its true character, showing that it is no righteousness.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:13
segments: Companies; literally "gatherings," thy idol-gods and foreign alliances.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:14
segments: And shall say; he shall see the highway for Israel's redemption in preparation, and shall exhort all God's servants to cooperate in the work of completing it.  See note on

entries.title: Isaiah 57:15
segments: Though heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, his chosen temple is the soul of the humble and contrite; and his blessed presence fills it with light and peace and strength.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:16
segments: For the spirit should fail before me; were I to deal with my people after their sins, they could not endure my wrath.
The best of men could not endure God's wrath for a moment, were he to deal with them in strict justice.  Our only hope is in his mercy through Christ.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:17
segments: The shame and guilt of men's wickedness belongs to them; but the glory of their repentance and obedience to God alone.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:18
segments:
I have seen his ways; his ways of perverseness. 
 
  Heal him; convert him, and thus restore him to my favor.  The doctrine here taught is, that God will have mercy upon his people for his own name's sake, and not for their sake.

entries.title: Isaiah 57:19
segments:
The fruit of the lips; thanksgiving and praise for salvation. 
 
  Far off--near; to all the penitent of Israel, at home and abroad. 
 
vv 19-21. 
 
God knows how to distinguish between the righteous and the wicked in his visible church.  To the former he will give peace and comfort in this life, and in the life to come glory everlasting; but the latter shall have disquietude here, and inherit "shame and everlasting contempt."

entries.title: Isaiah 57:20
segments: The wicked; the wicked in Israel, such as have been described in this chapter.  But the words apply to all wicked men.
